title: Henri IV to Andre Hurault de Maisse, ambassador at Venice, 8 February and 27 April 1593, in Maisse's Cipher (1592-1593) (BnF fr. 16093 ff. 406, 410)

system.summary: Maisse's Cipher (1592-1593), the key Henri IV also sent to Savary de Breves: letter-shaped symbols for the letters, homophonic, with two-digit figures for a nomenclator of common words and names.
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's reconstruction 'Maisse' Cipher 2 (BnF fr.16093, f.344 etc.)' (henryiv_Maisse2.png), applied unchanged to six stretches (128 signs) of ff. 404, 406, 410 on 27 Oct 2026; ff. 398, 401, 402, 404 of the same volume carry partial interlinear decipherments
system.notes: Word codes on Tomokiyo's table include vous, ceulx, est, faict, de, des, fort, par, pour, que, qui, advis, ces, comme, bon, avec, et, jay, les, luy, moy. f. 404 says in clear that Maisse kept 'le double du chiffre que j'ay envoye aud. de Breves'. Commonest figures on f. 404: 27, 10, 26, 23, 19, 21, 22, 24, 8.

prior_solution.where: contemporary clear copies of both letters in Brienne 13 (NAF 6984) fol. 171r and 193v; f. 406's twin f. 404 carries a partial interlinear decipherment; Tomokiyo's key for the cipher published as an image on cryptiana; no reading of ff. 406/410 published

conditions.human_role: Project-level only: the target was taken from the repository's catalogue and worked by the model in Claude Code; no target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Tomokiyo's Henri IV page re-read as HTML rather than as the text dump in research/gallica_sweep/src: the four leaves fall in two different cipher sections, each with siblings in the same volume, so the entry's class B and 'no sibling found' were both wrong.
fr. 16093 resolved to ark btv1b90074656 by Gallica SRU and the folio-to-canvas offsets calibrated by reading folio numbers off the leaves.

The old Harlay piece numbers 247 (f. 406) and 251 (f. 410) matched to Berger de Xivrey's citations, which give clear copies in fonds Brienne 13 = NAF 6984 (fol. 171r, 193v); located on the images by heading and preamble.
Tomokiyo's key image for this cipher (henryiv_Maisse2.png, 'Maisse' Cipher 2 (BnF fr.16093, f.344 etc.)') fetched from his page; not applied to ff. 406/410.

ff. 406 and 410 read from the Brienne clear copies; f. 406 shown to be the duplicate of f. 404 (same date, same opening, one Brienne copy), so its text is also attested by f. 404's interlinear decipherment; f. 412 is the duplicate of f. 410.

Novelty re-examined after Lasry's note on 'undeciphered'. G. Lasry (21 Sept 2026): on cryptiana 'undeciphered' means no interlinear or nearby deciphered copy, not unsolved; unsolved material is on the unsolved page. The page no longer says Tomokiyo 'never applied' his keys; the claim is a published reading only.

Entry split on 14 Oct 2026 under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026) from maisse1592, which had joined ff. 370/373 (Maisse's Cipher of 1592) with ff. 406/410 (Maisse's Cipher of 1592-93, the Breves cipher). This profile keeps ff. 406 and 410 (Maisse's Cipher of 1592-93) only.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): no transcription or decryption of ff. 406/410 exists in the repository (the text was read from the Brienne 13 clear copies, not transcribed); entries link the Gallica images of the cipher leaves (and twin f. 404) and of the Brienne copies.

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): no text of f. 406 or f. 410 is in the repository (images and links only). Both relabelled decoded, not read; class read -> not read; method read from existing decipherment -> not solved, until the Brienne 13 copies are transcribed.
Consistency pass (cl): documents[].read for f406, f410 read -> not read, matching outcome.texts (decoded, not read) and fraction_read_source.

WAINUT contribution: Brienne 13 (NAF 6984, btv1b100904592) canvases 176-178, 199-200 and the cipher leaves fr. 16093 (btv1b90074656) canvases 455, 457, 458, 461 viewed at full resolution (Gallica viewer and the BnF IIIF API at openapi.bnf.fr); no image kept in the repository.

WAINUT contribution: the clear copies transcribed line by line: fol. 171r (lower part) to 172v for f. 406 (wainut/f406_brienne_copy.txt) and fol. 193v, 194r and the first lines of 194v for f. 410 (wainut/f410_brienne_copy.txt). fol. 173r and the rest of 194v are not transcribed. The top of fol. 171r ('insollence des Espagnolz ... prier Dieu, etc.') was found to be the end of Maisse's own letter 'Au Roy du dixiesme Avril 1593' (heading on fol. 170v), not part of the King's letter of 8 Feb.

WAINUT contribution: the start of each cipher block fixed against the copies (f. 406 and twin f. 404: 'Le surplus de voz lettres ...', right after 'vous y pouvez apporter', on the same line of the leaf; f. 410: 'L'experience a faict cognoistre ...', after 'de ma bonne grace et faveur'). Six stretches (f. 410 cipher ll. 1-2, f. 404 l. 3, f. 406 cipher l. 1 and two pieces of l. 2; 128 signs) transcribed sign by sign (wainut/cipher_lines.txt) and decrypted with Tomokiyo's 'Maisse' Cipher 2' unchanged: they give the copy's text (wainut/f406_decryption.md, f410_decryption.md). Word signs 15 = faict, 17 = vous, 18 = est confirmed.

WAINUT contribution: wainut/decode_check.py: difflib ratio of decryption to copy 0.79-1.00 on the six stretches (0.91-0.94 on the three longest, 25-39 signs; 0.79 on the 13-sign stretch with two holes); 2000 random permutations of the key values give at most 0.67 on any stretch and 0.53 on the four longest; 2000 shuffles of the group order at most 0.65 on the three longest and 0.71 on the 13-sign stretch.

WAINUT contribution: a second, independent look at the images corrected the first sign-level alignment: on f. 404 the '9' is the uy sign (u) and the '+' the theta-like d; on f. 410 '9t' is c (not n), 's-long + hook' is two signs (e, n) and the z-like sign is a; the hooked q-like sign for l is in Tomokiyo's l column (not a new homophone); the cipher spells 'cougnoistre' and 'que vous en avez'; the copy has 'vous estes estes'. Still open: three signs where the copy has 'vous ne' decode r u e; the pi-like sign in 'Rome' and the '+' in 'voiage' do not fit the key.

WAINUT contribution, review fixes (PR #106): the two WAINUT texts entries replace the earlier f406/f410 entries (no duplicate doc ids), documents[].read, class, method, gaps and escalation brought in line; the self-assigned reading_review grades removed. Status in progress: the copies' fol. 173r and 194v and the remaining cipher lines are the next step.

Brienne 13 fol. 173r-173v and 194v-196r transcribed (the copies' ends); fol. 172r-173v and 193v-196r read a second time, blind, and collated: 66 disagreements, 63 settled on the image (beling/transcription/, second_reading/collation.tsv). (Andrew Beling, beling/)

Round 1: three blind sign-by-sign transcriptions, made without the copies, of f. 406r ll. 13 and 23-43, f. 406v ll. 1-20 and f. 410r ll. 10-31 (2,501 test signs; beling/transcription/). (Andrew Beling, beling/)

Pre-registered (beling/PREREG.md): Tomokiyo's key frozen from his image, scored against the copies on the round-1 lines: 0.818 (pass needed 0.85); 200 shuffled keys best 0.230, margin 0.589. A fail by the rule: sign naming and one key value (pi). (Andrew Beling, beling/)

A shared sign catalogue made blind to the copies (89 signs; beling/catalogue/), and 198 round-1 tokens renamed on the leaves (round1_catalogue/changes.tsv). Round 2: three new blind readers transcribed f. 406v ll. 21-33, f. 410v, f. 411r and f. 411v ll. 1-3 (3,543 signs). Both cipher blocks now complete: 6,238 signs. (Andrew Beling, beling/)

Pre-registered (beling/PREREG_round2.md): a key rebuilt mechanically from the round-1 lines by a fixed rule and frozen (key/key_v2.tsv); on the 84 held-out lines 0.894 (bar 0.85), 200 shuffled keys best 0.149, margin 0.745. Pass. Tomokiyo's key on the same signs 0.801. (Andrew Beling, beling/)

Full construction from all lines against the corrected copies, after the test (beling/key/key_full.tsv, construction_overrides.tsv): Tomokiyo's key confirmed for 43 signs; pi = o (not r; settles 'rrme' as Rome), the zeta-like sign = et (not y); 13 signs not in his key valued from the copies (k = a, 238 places; 6~ ss; La faire; va ll; Cloop g ...); 9 values judged. 0.908 of decrypted letters match the copies. (Andrew Beling, beling/)

Both letters decrypted in full and set line by line against the copies (beling/results/full_decryption.txt); wording variants listed (full_variants.tsv), e.g. f. 411v 'il est possible que Dieu pourra amener' for the copy's 'peut estre que Dieu amenera'. The short run on f. 406r l. 13 reads 'pour [le] regard des presens' (copy: 'pour le regard du pape'). (Andrew Beling, beling/)

outcome.method_basis: The text of both letters is taken from the contemporary clear copies in fonds Brienne 13 (BnF NAF 6984), located through the Harlay piece numbers and Berger de Xivrey (PR #7) and transcribed on 27 Oct 2026 except fol. 173r and most of fol. 194v. Tomokiyo's key, applied unchanged to the first cipher stretches (128 signs), gives the copies' text, so the copies carry the reading of the cipher. Proposed for the maintainer: class read in part, method read from existing decipherment; work in progress (Remaining gaps). 11-12 Nov 2026 (beling/): the cipher itself is now transcribed and decrypted sign by sign on both leaves, with Tomokiyo's key corrected and extended from the leaves; the copies now carry the reading only where a sign is doubtful.
outcome.notes: The fraction is the content obtained from the clear copies; no group of ff. 406/410 was transcribed or deciphered with the key here, so the cipher itself is not verified on these leaves. Split 14 Oct 2026 from maisse1592. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: the Brienne copies are not transcribed; both letters decoded, not read; class read -> not read, method -> not solved until they are. 27 Oct 2026 (WAINUT): the copies transcribed except fol. 173r and most of fol. 194v, and Tomokiyo's key applied to the first cipher stretches (128 signs); class not read -> read in part, method not solved -> read from existing decipherment, proposed; in progress. 11-12 Nov 2026 (Andrew Beling, beling/): both cipher blocks transcribed blind (6,238 signs); Tomokiyo's key 0.818 on round 1 (fail); a key rebuilt from round 1 passed on 84 held-out lines (0.894, margin 0.745); full construction in beling/key/key_full.tsv (0.908 of decrypted letters match the copies); copies finished and read twice. Class read proposed in NOTES (Assumptions); left at read in part here until a reviewer agrees.

texts.label: f. 406 (twin f. 404), Chartres, 8 Feb 1593, from the Brienne 13 clear copy; cipher decrypted on its first lines (WAINUT, 27 Oct 2026)
texts.summary: Henri IV to Maisse at Venice: he has answered every despatch and noted their dates, approves Maisse's sending of duplicates, hopes the despatch for the Pope was not delayed, and has written to the Grand Seigneur and his ministers (Maisse can read the letter to Breves if he kept the copy of the cipher). From the start of the cipher block on (its end is not fixed): Rome; Pisany's arrival in Italy; the war in Piedmont and a letter sent through Lesdiguieres' men with a further charge for Lesdiguieres; Gondi at Nancy with the King's passport; the King going down to Saumur, where his sister is. The earlier summary of f. 406 in this entry and in NOTES (the Spanish insolence, Pisany and Cardinal Gondi not to leave Rome) describes the top of fol. 171r, which is the end of Maisse's own letter to the King of 10 Apr 1593. (Maintainer spot-check of Brienne 13 canvas 176 pending.)
texts.note: Read in part: the letter's end (Brienne 13 fol. 173r) and the end of the cipher block are not transcribed, and only the start of the cipher block (four stretches, 56 signs) is transcribed and decrypted. read_share is not given because the share of the whole letter is not known. The copy's lines checked a second time, independently: the heading and opening on fol. 171r and the line 'Le surplus de voz lettres ... du voiage'; the rest is one reading. Images: cipher leaf f. 406 https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/btv1b90074656/f457.item, twin f. 404 https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/btv1b90074656/f455.item, Brienne 13 copy https://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/btv1b100904592/f176.item. Replaces the earlier entry (decoded, not read, images only; reading audit 22 Oct 2026). No reading_review: grading is left to a reviewer. 12 Nov 2026 (Andrew Beling, beling/): the copy is now transcribed to the end (fol. 173r-v) and read twice; the cipher block is fixed at leaf ll. 23-43 of the recto and ll. 1-33 of the verso (54 lines, 2,243 signs), all transcribed blind and decrypted (beling/results/full_decryption.txt, letter 406; the verso lines are in round2/f406v_411v_cipher.tsv up to l. 33). Not yet: a translation of the whole letter and a reading_review, so the state stays read in part. 12 Nov 2026: reading and translation now point to beling/reading_f406.md and translation_f406.md, which give the whole letter (WAINUT's partial files remain in wainut/, unchanged).

reading_review.by: Andrew Beling, with two independent AI-agent readings (Claude)
reading_review.note: Read as sentences, 12 Nov 2026. The whole letter reads as coherent French. For the part in cipher the words are those of the contemporary clear copy (corrected by our second reading of it); our own sign-by-sign decryption is unspaced and matches that copy at 0.91 of letters, with single-sign misreadings and a few real wording variants (noted in the reading). Coherent but normalised from a raw decode: B.

texts.label: f. 410 (twin f. 412), Mantes, 27/28 Apr 1593, from the Brienne 13 clear copy; cipher decrypted on its first two lines (WAINUT, 27 Oct 2026)
texts.summary: Henri IV acknowledges Maisse's letters of 20 Feb, 7 and 23 Mar (one courier held by the duc de Nevers in Champagne) and assures him that his absence will cost him nothing. In cipher: experience has proved Maisse right about the affairs of Rome; on advice the King will not yet recall Cardinal de Gondi or the marquis de Pisany, to keep the Pope from extremes, and leaves their moves to the Grand Duke's advice; Gondi's promises. Then (whether still in cipher is not fixed): the original letters of the Grand Seigneur and his ministers received; the King waits on the ambassador's despatch.
